tasks.title: Build a labeled Series
tasks.statement: Create a Series from the dict and print its values as a list.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series({"a": 1, "b": 2})
print(s.tolist())

tasks.title: Label alignment leaves a gap
tasks.statement: Add the two Series and print how many values ended up missing.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.Series([1, 2], index=["x", "y"])
b = pd.Series([10, 20], index=["y", "z"])
print(int((a + b).isna().sum()))

tasks.title: Read by label
tasks.statement: Print the value stored under the label "y".
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([5, 6], index=["x", "y"])
print(s["y"])

tasks.title: Count above the mean
tasks.statement: Print how many values are strictly above the mean.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2, 3, 4])
print(int((s > s.mean()).sum()))

debug.title: A label read from a default index
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([5, 6])
print(s["a"])
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([5, 6])
print(s.iloc[0])
debug.error: KeyError: 'a'

debug.title: Two values, one label
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2], index=["a"])
print(s.tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2], index=["a", "b"])
print(s.tolist())
debug.error: ValueError: Length of values (2) does not match length of index (1)

debug.title: The removed append method
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2])
print(s.append(3).tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2])
print(pd.concat([s, pd.Series([3])], ignore_index=True).tolist())
debug.error: AttributeError: 'Series' object has no attribute 'append'

debug.title: Sum of numeric-looking text
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(["1", "2"])
print(s.sum())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series(["1", "2"]).astype(int)
print(s.sum())
debug.error: Wrong output: 12 — object dtypes concatenate text, so the sum is a string, not 3.

tasks.title: Frame from records
tasks.statement: Build the frame from the list of dicts and print its shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame([{"a": 1, "b": 2}, {"a": 3, "b": 4}])
print(df.shape)

tasks.title: Custom index at construction
tasks.statement: Create the frame with the given index and print the index labels.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"v": [1, 2]}, index=["r1", "r2"])
print(df.index.tolist())

tasks.title: A derived column
tasks.statement: Add a column that is the sum of the two existing columns and print it.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [3, 4]})
df["total"] = df["a"] + df["b"]
print(df["total"].tolist())

tasks.title: Column types after construction
tasks.statement: Print the column names and the number of numeric columns.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": ["x"], "c": [1.5]})
print(df.columns.tolist(), len(df.select_dtypes("number").columns))

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [1]})
print(df.shape)
debug.fix:

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [1, 2]})

debug.title: All scalar values without an index
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": 1, "b": 2})
print(df.shape)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2]})

debug.title: Too few names for the columns
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2]})
df.columns = ["only"]
print(df.columns.tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2]})
df.columns = ["one", "two"]
print(df.columns.tolist())

debug.title: Rows reported as cells
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6]})
print(len(df))
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6]})
print(df.size)
debug.error: Wrong output: 3 — len() counts rows, while the table has 6 cells.

tasks.title: Shape and columns
tasks.statement: Print the shape and the column list of the frame.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2]})
print(df.shape, df.columns.tolist())

tasks.title: Select two columns
tasks.statement: Select the two numeric columns and print the resulting shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2], "c": ["x"]})
print(df[["a", "b"]].shape)

tasks.title: Label slice versus position slice
tasks.statement: Print the row count from a label slice of 0:1 and from a position slice of 0:1.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [10, 20, 30]})
print(len(df.loc[0:1]), len(df.iloc[0:1]))

tasks.title: Types as text
tasks.statement: Print each column's dtype as a string.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [1.5], "c": ["x"]})
print(df.dtypes.astype(str).tolist())

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})
print(df.shape())

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})

tasks.title: Filter and count
tasks.statement: Print how many rows have a value above 2.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"v": [1, 3, 5]})
print(int((df["v"] > 2).sum()))

tasks.title: Targeted assignment
tasks.statement: Set b to 0 where a is above 1, then print b.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [9, 9]})
df.loc[df["a"] > 1, "b"] = 0
print(df["b"].tolist())

tasks.title: Two conditions in query
tasks.statement: Use query to keep 1 < a < 4 and print the kept values.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3, 4]})
print(df.query("1 < a < 4")["a"].tolist())

tasks.title: Filter with isin
tasks.statement: Keep only the listed cities and print them in order.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune", "Delhi", "Goa"]})
print(df[df["city"].isin(["Pune", "Goa"])]["city"].tolist())

debug.title: and instead of &
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [5, 1]})
print(df[(df["a"] > 0) and (df["b"] < 5)])
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [5, 1]})
print(df[(df["a"] > 0) & (df["b"] < 5)].shape)
debug.error: ValueError: The truth value of a Series is ambiguous. Use a.empty, a.bool(), a.item(), a.any() or a.all().

debug.title: Comparing numbers with text

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
print(df[df["a"] > "1"].shape)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
print(df[df["a"] > 1].shape)
debug.error: TypeError: Invalid comparison between dtype=int64 and str

debug.title: A query variable that does not exist
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
print(df.query("a > @limit").shape)
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2]})
limit = 1
print(df.query("a > @limit").shape)
debug.error: pandas.errors.UndefinedVariableError: local variable 'limit' is not defined

debug.title: A filter that was never assigned
debug.broken:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [9, 9]})
df[df["a"] > 1]["b"] = 0
print(df["b"].tolist())
debug.fix:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [9, 9]})
df.loc[df["a"] > 1, "b"] = 0
print(df["b"].tolist())
debug.error: Wrong output: [9, 9] — chained assignment writes into a temporary copy, so the frame is unchanged.

tasks.title: Parse with an explicit format
tasks.statement: Parse the date string and print its year.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.to_datetime("31/01/2026", format="%d/%m/%Y")
print(s.year)

tasks.title: Weekday of a date
tasks.statement: Print the weekday number for 2026-01-05.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.to_datetime("2026-01-05")
print(s.dayofweek)

tasks.title: Three daily timestamps
tasks.statement: Build a three-period daily range and print its first and last date.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

r = pd.date_range("2026-01-01", periods=3, freq="D")
print(r[0].strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), r[-1].strftime("%Y-%m-%d"))

tasks.title: Month extraction
tasks.statement: Print the month number of every timestamp in the series.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.to_datetime(pd.Series(["2026-01-15", "2026-03-01"]))
print(s.dt.month.tolist())
